CE_1.subject: Physics

modules.title: Module 1: Quantum Mechanics
topics: Wave nature of particles, Uncertainty principle, Wave function and wave packets, Time dependent & time independent Schrodinger equation, Solution of Schrödinger’s equation for one dimensional problem: Particle in a box

modules.title: Module 2: Solid, Semiconductors and Superconductivity
topics: Kronig Penny Model (Qualitative), Origin of energy bands: Metals, Semiconductors and Insulators, Solar Cell, LED, Hall effect. Properties of Superconductors

Meissner effect, Critical Magnetic Field, Isotope effect, Persistent current, Magnetic levitation, Type-1 & Type-2 superconductors and their comparison, BCS theory of superconductivity (qualitative only)

modules.title: Module 3: Lasers, Fiber Optics and Acoustics
topics: Induced absorption, spontaneous and stimulated emission, Einstein’s coefficients, population inversion, pumping, meta-stable state, principle of LASER, characteristics of a laser beam, Gas (He-Ne) laser, Applications of lasers

Optical fibre -Principle and Structure, Propagation of light in optical fibres, Numerical aperture and angle of acceptance, Classification of optical fibres, Single mode and Multimode optical fibers, Step Index and Graded Index optical fibres, Optical fibre communication system (Block diagram only)

Weber-Fetchner law, Reverberation & Reverberation time, Sabine’s formula for reverberation time (Derivation not required), Absorption co-efficient, Factors affecting acoustics of buildings and their remedies, Acoustic design of a hall

modules.title: Module 4: Electromagnetism and Dielectric Materials
topics: Non polar and Polar molecules, Dielectrics, Dielectric polarization and its types, Polarizability of a ⃗, 𝑃⃗ and 𝐸⃗, Gauss law in dielectrics, Clausius-Mossotti relation, Frequency dielectric, Relation between 𝐷 dependence of dielectric constant
Introduction to Gradient, Divergence and Curl, Laplace’s and Poisson’s equation for electrostatic potential
Continuity equation for current densities, Displacement current, Maxwell’s equations with significance, Maxwell’s equation in vacuum and non-conducting medium

modules.title: Module 5: Mechanics and Low Temperature Physics
topics: Elasticity, Relations among elastic constants, twisting couple on a wire, bending of beams with symmetric cross-section, Cantilever. Non-inertial frames of reference
Rotating co-ordinate system, Five-term acceleration formula, Centripetal and Coriolis accelerations

Applications: Weather systems, Foucault pendulum. Joule-Thomson effect, Liquefaction of air: Linde process, Liquefaction of helium, Adiabatic demagnetization, He-3 Cryostat. CSE_4.subject: Database Management System Lab
experiments: Basic SQL – DDL, DML, DQL (CO1)
Create tables with primary and foreign key constraints using DDL commands.
Perform INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE operations using DML commands.
Retrieve data using SELECT with WHERE, ORDER BY, and GROUP BY clauses.
Use SQL aggregate functions: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX. Advanced SQL – Joins, Views, Nested Queries (CO2)
Write queries using various types of JOINs (INNER, OUTER, SELF).
Implement nested queries and correlated subqueries.
Create and query VIEWS.
Define and enforce constraints (CHECK, NOT NULL, UNIQUE). ER Design & Normalization (CO3)
Draw an ER diagram for a given scenario and convert it into relational schema.
Identify functional dependencies and apply 1NF, 2NF, 3NF.
Apply BCNF decomposition to a relational schema. Transactions, Indexing, Recovery (CO4)
Simulate transactions using COMMIT, ROLLBACK, and SAVEPOINT.
Implement basic concurrency control using locking mechanism (simulated).
Simulate log-based recovery (theoretical or pseudo-code).
Create indexes on a table and measure performance differences with and without indexing.
Install MongoDB and create a database and collection.
Perform CRUD operations on MongoDB documents.
Use MongoDB aggregation operations (match, group, sort).
Model nested/embedded documents to represent relationships.

Import JSON data into MongoDB and perform queries using Mongo Shell or Compass. Additional Experiments: Additional experiments (if any) considered appropriate by the department may be conducted. Text /

ME_5.subject: Fluid Mechanics-II

modules.title: Module 1: Viscous Flow
topics: Governing equations: Definition of Laminar and turbulent flow, Reynolds number, Continuity and momentum conservation (Navier-Stokes) equations in Cartesian, cylindrical (polar) and spherical coordinates

Internal incompressible flow: Exact solution of NS equation: Fully developed laminar flow between infinite parallel plates (Plane Poiseuille and Couette flow), Fully developed laminar flow through circular pipes

Flow through pipes: Pressure drop, losses of energy due to friction, Darcy-Weisbach equation for losses of head in pipes, empirical formula for coefficient of friction, major and minor losses in pipes, equivalent pipe, flow through series and parallel pipes

Boundary layer theory: Boundary layer equation, Blasius flow over flat plate, Wall shear and boundary layer thickness, Von Karman momentum integral equation for boundary layer, Separation of boundary layer, Control of boundary layer separation, Mechanics of boundary layer transition, several events of transition, Form drag and skin friction drag

modules.title: Module 2: Turbulent Flow
topics: Characteristics & Governing Equations: Characteristics and classification of turbulence, mean motion and fluctuations (Reynolds decomposition), derivation of governing equations for turbulent flow (Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes), concept of Reynolds stresses, and boundary conditions
Turbulence Modeling & Velocity Profiles: Prandtl’s mixing length theory, universal velocity distribution law (viscous sublayer, buffer layer, and turbulent core), shear velocity
